title: Unauthenticated Kubernetes Dashboard Exposing Cluster Management and Secret Tokens
description: Publicly exposed Kubernetes Dashboard accessible without credentials, providing cluster-admin privileges to browse namespaces and retrieve secrets.
impact: Full cluster compromise allowing attackers to read confidential environment variables, pull proprietary container images, and execute arbitrary commands in cluster pods.
remediation: Restrict dashboard access behind an authenticated reverse proxy or VPN, enable RBAC authentication, and disable public ingress routing.
steps_to_reproduce:
1. Navigate to https://dashboard.example.com in browser or curl.
2. Observe dashboard UI loading without any authentication prompt.
3. Verify access by checking pod list in default namespace via /api/v1/namespaces.

attack_path.step: Attacker navigates to publicly routable dashboard subdomain
Kubernetes dashboard UI loads without requiring authentication
Attacker queries cluster pods and secrets through web API
Extracted tokens allow arbitrary remote command execution across cluster nodes

title: Publicly Accessible Git Metadata Exposing Application Source Code and Configuration
description: The .git repository directory is exposed via web server misconfiguration, allowing extraction of source files and committed credentials.
impact: Complete source code disclosure enabling discovery of hardcoded API secrets, architectural flaws, and internal service credentials.
remediation: Block web server access to dotfiles like .git in Nginx or Apache configuration rules immediately.
steps_to_reproduce:
1. Execute curl -sI https://api.example.com/.git/HEAD.
2. Observe HTTP 200 OK response with body containing 'ref: refs/heads/master'.
3. Confirm exposure of index and object store files.

attack_path.step: Attacker requests /.git/HEAD on the public production host
Web server returns repository head reference without authentication
Attacker dumps repository objects to reconstruct complete source tree
